data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of non-experts following a checklist is more reliable than a single expert because the checklist acts as a 'variance floor', eliminating the catastrophic 'black swan' failures of expert intuition while the panel's collective oversight prevents the 'blind obedience' failure of a single non-expert.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task requires 'synthesis' (connecting disparate dots) rather than 'analysis' (checking a list of requirements).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist contains a systemic error that the expert's intuition would have naturally bypassed.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel suffers from 'social loafing' where members assume others have verified the checklist items.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The 'Variance Floor' mechanism: Expert intuition is a high-mean but high-variance process (prone to idiosyncratic blind spots). A checklist is a low-mean but ultra-low-variance process. In tasks with objectively verifiable outcomes, the panel's role is not to 'solve' the problem but to 'verify the execution' of the checklist, effectively turning the task into a series of binary checks where the probability of collective failure is lower than the probability of a single expert's cognitive lapse.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
